original_question: Let F = {a1(t), ..., aℓ(t)} be Hardy-field functions of polynomial growth. Is the family of integer sequences {[a1(n)], ..., [aℓ(n)]} good for ℓ-convergence of a single transformation exactly when every nontrivial linear combination a in span*(F) either stays farther than logarithmic scale from every real multiple of an integer polynomial, or differs from some real multiple of an integer polynomial by a finite limit, or stays within O(log t) of t/m for some nonzero integer m?
target_in_paper: Section 6.1.1, Problem 22 in the arXiv v3 paper (the Hardy-field single-transformation ℓ-convergence criterion; the same statement appears as Problem 19 in older pagination excerpts).
correct_elements: Your draft is very close to the paper’s intended problem. It correctly targets the Hardy-field section on powers of a single transformation, uses a family F = {a1,...,aℓ} of polynomial-growth Hardy-field functions, asks for an if-and-only-if characterization of when the integer-part sequences {([a1(n)]),...,([aℓ(n)])} are good for ℓ-convergence of a single transformation, and it already reproduces the paper’s three alternative behaviors for every nontrivial linear combination a ∈ span*(F): logarithmic separation from every real multiple of an integer polynomial, convergence to a real multiple of an integer polynomial up to a finite real limit, or logarithmic closeness to t/m.
missing_details: The functions a1(t),...,aℓ(t) must belong to a common Hardy field, not merely each to some Hardy field.

The paper’s local convention is that F consists of functions of polynomial growth; this should be made explicit as each ai growing at most polynomially (in the paper’s older pagination snippet: ai(t)/t^k → 0 for some k ∈ N).
span*(F) must be defined explicitly as the set of all nonzero real linear combinations of the functions in F.
The notation [x] should be identified as the integer part of x.

The phrase “good for ℓ-convergence of a single transformation” must be expanded: for every invertible measure preserving system (X, 𝓧, μ, T) and every f1,...,fℓ ∈ L∞(μ), the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T^{[a1(n)]}f1 ··· T^{[aℓ(n)]}fℓ converge in L^2(μ) as N → ∞.
Condition (i) should be stated exactly as |a(t) − c p(t)|/log t → ∞ for every c ∈ R and every p ∈ Z[t].
Condition (ii) should be stated exactly as a(t) − c p(t) → d for some c,d ∈ R and some p ∈ Z[t].
Condition (iii) should be stated exactly as |a(t) − t/m| ≪ log t for some integer m ≠ 0.
It should be explicit that the problem concerns one single transformation T used in all factors, not several commuting transformations.
The paper states this as an open problem (“Show that ... if and only if ...”), not as a proved theorem.
refined_question: Let ℓ ∈ N, let F = {a1(t), ..., aℓ(t)} be functions of polynomial growth from a common Hardy field, let span*(F) denote the set of all nonzero real linear combinations of a1,...,aℓ, and let [x] denote the integer part of x. Is it true that the collection of integer sequences {([a1(n)]), ..., ([aℓ(n)])} is good for ℓ-convergence of a single transformation—that is, for every invertible measure preserving system (X, 𝓧, μ, T) and every f1,...,fℓ ∈ L∞(μ), the averages (1/N) Σ_{n=1}^N T^{[a1(n)]}f1 ··· T^{[aℓ(n)]}fℓ converge in L^2(μ) as N → ∞—if and only if every a ∈ span*(F) satisfies at least one of the following three conditions: (i) |a(t) − c p(t)|/log t → ∞ for every c ∈ R and p ∈ Z[t]; or (ii) a(t) − c p(t) → d for some c,d ∈ R and p ∈ Z[t]; or (iii) |a(t) − t/m| ≪ log t for some integer m ≠ 0?
justification: The draft is trying to capture the Hardy-field convergence problem in Section 6.1.1, not the earlier general-sequences or polynomial sections. The official target is the open problem that asks for necessary and sufficient conditions for ℓ-convergence of the collection {([a1(n)]),...,([aℓ(n)])}; your three alternatives match the paper’s bullets exactly in substance. The nearby preceding theorem gives the single-sequence prototype with the same three alternatives, and the earlier convergence definition supplies the exact meaning of “good for ℓ-convergence of a single transformation.” I therefore kept your question narrow, retained the iff structure, and only added the hidden quantifiers, notation, and ergodic-theoretic definition needed to make it fully stand-alone and faithful to the paper.
